subject: trying to program a linear interpolation (or something smoother would be even better)

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: trying to program a linear interpolation (or something smoother would be even better)
parts:
Hi, I'm trying to put in a log-prior that I'm defining as a piecewise-linear function. Something like this:

theta is a real parameter defined on [0,1].
I specify as data the values of p(theta) up to a normalizing constant at the values 0, 1/K, 2/K, ..., 1. Call this vector[K+1] log_prior;
We can have the log-prior be piecewise linear connecting these points. (Actually I'd like to have continuous derivatives too but maybe for now we forget about that?)

In Stan I want to use target += to assign this prior for theta.

I was thinking of doing something like this:

index <- ceil(theta*K); // I'm not so sure on this because floor and ceil return reals, and I want an integer index.
fraction <- fmod(K*theta, 1);
target += (1 - fraction)*log_prior[index] + fraction*log_prior[index+1];

I guess we'd really want a spline here. Is this something that is perhaps worth doing, to hard-code splines in Stan?

In the meantime, is my above code ok or is there some better, more standard way of doing this?

Thx

A

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] trying to program a linear interpolation (or something smoother would be even better)
parts:
There's not a good way to do these in Stan. So yes,
it'd make sense to build them in. The log densities should
be continuously differentiable up to gradients anyway.

You can't use ceil() that way because it returns a real value.

You have to hack it in a loop or if-then-else chain.

We could build it in. The reason we don't want to do this
in general is that it lets people build log densities that
aren't continuously differentiable.

- Bob
